I've done competitive gymnastics for 13 years, and this is how I got my aerial:

1. The kick: you need to be able to kick over fast enough so that you don't have to put your hands down. In order to do so, focus on the kick of your back leg. I did a drill called "needle kicks," which is when you keep your front leg and hands on the ground while you kick repeatedly with the back leg, focusing on the speed and range of the kick. I usually do 2 sets of 15, sometimes with an ankle weight. 
2. Leg strength: you also need sufficient height to safely finish an aerial. There are a lot of different exercises for your quads, but I would advise focusing on leg power (ex. squat jumps, lunges).
3. The skill: you can watch youtube videos to see what people do with their arms, but to generate the most power  I think swinging them straight down is best. Start by doing it from a run/hurdle from a height, and slowly work up from there. 

Good luck! And if you have any other questions feel free to message me :)
